root_idea.summary: The root centers on drawing near, becoming imminent, and temporal or spatial proximity.
root_idea.development: The basic notion of nearness develops into the imminence of an event or time, hastening, reciprocal approach, and physical compactness or narrowness; related figurative uses extend narrowness to disposition.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed as the singular feminine active participle, used substantively in Quranic eschatological expressions.

senses.definition: To draw near or become imminent.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the subject is the Resurrection: it has drawn near and become imminent.

senses.definition: An approaching or imminent eschatological event, especially the Resurrection.
senses.usage_conditions: A feminine active participle used substantively, normally with the definite article. In 53:57 it denotes the approaching Resurrection; in يوم الآزفة in 40:18 it denotes the imminent event or day, interpreted variously as the Resurrection, the perilous event of nearing Hell, or death.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten or be quick; to draw near while hastening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Form I verbal use distinct from the Quranic event-imminence use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hastening, quick, or intent on hastening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective or active participle applied to someone characterized by haste; the source’s human example is illustrative, not restrictive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incite or urge someone to hasten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV construction, attested with a personal object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stepping with contracted or shortened steps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V verbal noun describing a particular manner of walking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw near together, one person or group to another.
Short or compact in build, with the several parts close together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical description based on contracted or closely set form.
A spatial use of the same lexical form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a contracted step; characterized by short steps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction خَطْوٌ مُتَآزِفٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively narrow-minded or ill-tempered; weak or cowardly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from physical narrowness or contraction, not a physical description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dirty or foul places; a dirty place, especially one associated with a constricted space.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical derivative distinct from the Quranic form groups.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The core approach or imminence meaning is represented by the Quranic Form I sense.
The separate haste or quickness use is represented classically.

The adjective for a hasty or quick person is represented.

cautions: آزِفَة is a substantivized active participle in the Quran. Its reference in 40:18 has variant interpretations, including the Resurrection, an imminent perilous event, and death; these are preserved as interpretive applications of the approaching-event designation rather than as unrelated lexical forms.
